results.content: AI deepfake trends in 2025 and 2026 point to a cyber threat landscape where fraud attempts have surged 2,137% in three years, voice cloning now requires as little as three seconds of audio, and documented organizational losses exceed $1.28 billion. Arup lost $25.6 million when cyberattackers used deepfake video and voice cloning to impersonate the CFO across 15 wire transfers. [...] According to the Resemble AI 2025 Deepfake Threat Report, 1,567 verified deepfake incidents resulted in $1.28 billion in fraud losses globally, with the caveat that over 80% of incidents did not disclose financial damage, meaning the true toll is almost certainly higher. [...] According to the FBI's Internet Crime Report 2025, business email compromise losses reached $3.04 billion in the United States alone, virtually all routed through manager-level approvers, a pattern that mirrors how deepfake voice and video cyberattacks target the same approval chokepoints. Deloitte's Center for Financial Services separately projects generative AI-enabled banking fraud in the United States climbing from a $12.3 billion baseline in 2023 to $40 billion by 2027.

results.title: Why do Experts Disagree on Existential Risk and P(doom)? A Survey of AI Experts
results.content: Several existing surveys have examined AI expert beliefs. The largest is the AI Impacts Survey(Grace et al., 2024), which surveys thousands of authors at the NeurIPS conference. AI Impacts asked experts questions such as “when will AI exceed human performance,” in response, the median expert answered 2061, and 10% answered 2026. According to AI Impacts, roughly 40% of respondents indicated a >10% chance of catastrophic outcomes from AI progress. Other surveys also seek to answer when experts [...] Prominent AI researchers hold dramatically different views on the degree of risk from building AGI. For example, Dr. Roman Yampolskiy estimates a 99% chance of an AI-caused existential catastrophe[Dr. Roman Yampolskiy [@romanyam] (2024)](#bib.bib4) (often called “P(doom)”) whereas others such as Yann Lecun believe that this probability is effectively zero[Yann LeCun [@ylecun] (2023)](#bib.bib5). The goal of the survey is to understand what drives this massive divergence in views on AI risk [...] My survey collected responses from 111 AI professionals across academia, industry, and AI safety research. rationale: Conditional on a binding, verified US–China cap on frontier AI R&D compute (comparable to a 25%-of-compute cap, in force through 2050), I reduce medium- and long-horizon tail risks substantially relative to baseline: this is the strongest risk-mitigating condition in the family, slowing frontier capability growth in both leading jurisdictions while redirecting compute to safety, so misalignment, AI-bio-uplift, and extreme-cyber probabilities at 2030–2100 are cut roughly 30–60% versus my unconditional estimates. Near-term, low-severity outcomes are largely unaffected because they are driven by already-deployed systems: documented AI-enabled fraud/deepfake losses are already ~$2–4B cumulatively and rising toward tens of billions per year, making the $1B AI rung near-certain and the $10B rung likely by 2028, with AI-enabled cyber campaigns (BEC, ransomware augmentation) the dominant contributor at the $1B–$100B levels. Bio and misalignment rungs remain rare events near-term (no historical AI-caused epidemic or mass-casualty loss-of-control incident), with probabilities growing over decades but damped by the cap; post-2050 lapse of the measure allows some risk re-acceleration in 2100 figures. Cross-cutting 10%-of-population catastrophe estimates are anchored on XPT expert/superforecaster ranges (AI extinction-level medians 0.3–3% by 2100), positioned toward the lower end given the condition, with the general catastrophe estimate dominated by non-AI causes (pandemic, nuclear) that the policy barely affects.
